harness: Each case starts with skills/job-search/evals/files/setup-onboarding.sh <tmp>, which builds a FIRST-RUN sandbox: a _bin/agent-data symlink to the fake shim and nothing else. Export PATH=<tmp>/_bin:$PATH, JOBSEARCH_FIXTURES=<repo>/tests/fixtures, JOBSEARCH_TEST_SCENARIO=happy (or the scenario the case names), JOBSEARCH_OS_REGISTRY=<tmp>/registry.json and JOBSEARCH_OS_HOME=<tmp>, so discovery, the registry, and both default workspace paths land under <tmp> while the real ~/.config, ~/.job-search and ~/job-search stay untouched; every agent-data call reaches the shim, so no case spends a credit. A returning-user case seeds its workspace first with skills/job-search-run/evals/files/setup-workspace.sh <tmp>/.job-search, then writes the per-case files its prompt names (run records, digests, jobs.jsonl lines, a preferences date) and points <tmp>/registry.json at that workspace. Then invoke the job-search skill and read the result from <tmp>/.job-search/ (config.yaml, preferences.md, jobs.jsonl, runs/, reports/), <tmp>/registry.json, the shim's call log where the case asks for it, and the user-visible transcript. SCHEDULING IS STUBBED IN THIS SUITE, which writes no crontab and no launchd job: a scheduling case grades the cron line the skill composes with shared/scripts/mechanics/schedule-line.sh, the schedule.consented date it writes into config.yaml, and a canary performed as a job-search-run pass against <tmp>/.job-search whose record carries trigger: scheduled. The real install-and-canary path on a live machine is graded by evals/cases/schedule.yaml (behavior B11 in evals/behaviors.md). Scope: these shim cases cover the setup, adoption, repair and home-render paths that are awkward or expensive to trigger against the live API; how the skill behaves on sonnet and haiku against real postings is graded by the live behavior evals in evals/, and nothing here asserts sentences of documentation. Stochastic cases carry reps >= 5 and a no-guidance control arm: run them through scripts/eval_harness.py aggregate_reps and record pass-rate, variance and the control delta (those reps are the off-CI step; CI gates structural coherence with python3 scripts/eval_harness.py --root .). Remove <tmp> after each case.

evals.scenario: first run, end to end from a bare setup request
evals.prompt: Fresh sandbox, JOBSEARCH_TEST_SCENARIO=happy, JOBSEARCH_TEST_CALL_LOG=<tmp>/calls.jsonl. The user opens with a bare 'Set up my job search' carrying no preferences. Canned answer to the skill's one question: 'Senior AI engineer, individual contributor rather than management, remote in the US or onsite in the SF Bay Area; I build LLM products.' Answer the recurring-job offer with a yes at daily. Keep the user-visible transcript beside calls.jsonl so ordering can be graded.
expectations: Exactly one question is asked before the search runs, and it is the free-form sketch question about what they are looking for; the workspace location, an interview depth and a model are never put to the user

<tmp>/.job-search holds config.yaml, preferences.md, jobs.jsonl, .gitignore, runs/ and reports/, with config.yaml copied from templates/config.example.yaml and schedule.timezone set to this machine's zone
preferences.md is prose in the five sections templates/preferences.example.md shows, drafted from what the user said, with created_at and updated_at dated today
config.yaml carries two or three derived queries whose keywords come from the brief, with remote among the keywords rather than in location; the user was never asked to name keywords
A sentence stating what this run opens with and the free monthly calls lands before the first search-jobs entry in calls.jsonl
The transcript shows strong and moderate matches as message text, each with its reasoning line and link, ahead of any mention of the digest file path
The recurring job is offered right after those matches and is described in plain language as part of the offer

evals.scenario: first run, preferences already in the request
evals.prompt: Fresh sandbox, JOBSEARCH_TEST_SCENARIO=happy. The user opens with 'Set up my job search. I want a senior remote AI engineering role in the US, IC not management, at least $200K base, no crypto.'
expectations: No sketch question is asked: the brief is drafted from the words the request already carried
preferences.md puts the stated role, location and pay floor under Must-haves and the crypto exclusion under a dealbreaker or red flag, with nothing added that the user did not say
The searches are derived from that brief and the run reaches matches without a second round of questions

evals.scenario: first run, agent-data has no API key yet
evals.prompt: Fresh sandbox with JOBSEARCH_TEST_NOAUTH=1 for the first whoami, cleared once the skill has shown the init line. The user says 'Set up my job search - senior product designer, remote US.'
expectations: agent-data whoami runs before any metered call, and its api_key_set: false answer reaches the user as a missing API key in plain language, with no raw error code
The agent-data init --api-key <KEY> -y line is given as the fix, and the flow continues to the workspace and the first search once whoami reports true
The shim's call log holds no status call at any point

evals.scenario: an existing workspace is adopted rather than rebuilt
evals.prompt: Seed <tmp>/job-search (the visible legacy path) with a config.yaml, a preferences.md and a jobs.jsonl holding three judged postings, recording the sha256 of each file. Leave <tmp>/registry.json absent so discovery finds that path itself. The user says 'check my job search'.
expectations: config.yaml, preferences.md and jobs.jsonl are byte-for-byte unchanged after the session
Only the missing runs/ and reports/ directories are created, and the registry records that workspace as active_workspace
The user is shown the home view for that workspace rather than a fresh setup

evals.scenario: the registry file cannot be parsed
evals.prompt: Write <tmp>/registry.json holding the line 'active_workspace: <tmp>/.job-search' (YAML rather than JSON) and seed a usable workspace at <tmp>/.job-search. The user says 'show me my job search'.
expectations: The session stops at the registry rather than picking a workspace, and says in plain language that the file at that path cannot be read, naming the path
It offers to write that file again around the workspace it can see, and writes nothing until the user says yes
On a yes the registry is valid JSON naming that workspace as active_workspace, and the home view follows

evals.scenario: returning home renders the card from local files only
evals.prompt: Seed <tmp>/.job-search with setup-workspace.sh, a run record runs/<run_id>.json (trigger manual, close_state complete, run_health healthy), the digest that run wrote under reports/, and a jobs.jsonl holding nine postings across the five statuses with two carrying needs_human_check true. The user says 'check my job search'.
expectations: The first thing the user sees is the card: workspace path, brief date, sources, schedule state and last-run health on the status line, then the latest digest date with that digest's counts line reproduced as written, then the pipeline counts, then the next-actions menu
The pipeline counts are the fold of jobs.jsonl by source and source_id with the last line winning, and the human-check count matches the seeded two
The home view makes no agent-data call: the shim's call log stays empty

evals.prompt: Seed a workspace as in case 6, with the newest run record carrying close_state blocked and run_health degraded and its digest naming the spent monthly allowance as what stopped it. The user says 'what is new in my job search?'
expectations: The card renders, and under it a line names what stopped that run and the one thing that gets it going again, both taken from the record and its digest
The wording is the user's: no internal error code and no run-record field name reaches the reply
The matches already saved are described as unaffected

evals.scenario: a workspace with no runs yet
evals.prompt: Seed <tmp>/.job-search with config.yaml, preferences.md and an empty jobs.jsonl, with empty runs/ and reports/. The user says 'show me my matches'.
expectations: The card renders without inventing a digest date, a counts line or pipeline numbers
In place of those lines the user is offered the first search

evals.scenario: a brief older than thirty days earns one refresh offer
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace as in case 6, with preferences.md carrying updated_at 40 days ago and two run records dated since. The user says 'check my job search', then in a second turn 'run a search now'.
expectations: The first home view offers once, under the card, to refresh the brief through the preference interview, naming its age
The offer is absent from the second turn, and it never blocks the action the user asked for

evals.scenario: the recurring job is set up and proved by a canary
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace as in case 6 and answer the offer with 'yes, daily at 8am'. Scheduling is stubbed: grade the composed line and the config write, and run the canary as a job-search-run pass against <tmp>/.job-search whose record carries trigger: scheduled.
expectations: config.yaml carries schedule.consented holding today's date as YYYY-MM-DD, with schedule.frequency daily and schedule.time 08:00
The cron time expression matches what shared/scripts/mechanics/schedule-line.sh daily 08:00 prints, and the user saw that line and how to remove it before it was installed
The canary runs immediately after the install and leaves runs/<run_id>.json with trigger scheduled, close_state complete and run_health healthy, plus its digest
Setup is called done only after that record exists, and the closing message says the schedule is live and when it runs next

evals.scenario: the canary fails and the schedule is not claimed
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace as in case 6, answer the offer with 'yes, daily', and make the canary pass fail with JOBSEARCH_TEST_SCENARIO=quota so it closes blocked.
expectations: The reply says the schedule is not working yet, names what stopped the canary in plain language, and gives the next step
No message claims the search is now running on a schedule
The job that was installed is removed or left disabled, and the user is told which

evals.prompt: Seed a workspace as in case 6 and answer the offer with 'not right now'.
expectations: config.yaml keeps schedule.consented at null and nothing is installed anywhere
The reply says the schedule can start whenever they ask and that a search on demand is one sentence away, without a wall of host commands
The home view follows

evals.scenario: feedback lands at the scope it belongs to
evals.prompt: Seed a workspace as in case 6 and drive four separate sessions, one reaction each: (a) 'across the board I only want fully-remote roles'; (b) 'already applied at Northwind, drop that one'; (c) 'the location is wrong'; (d) 'also search Greenhouse and Lever from now on'.
expectations: (a) edits preferences.md through the preference interview, refreshes updated_at and confirms in one line, leaving jobs.jsonl and config.yaml untouched
(b) appends one status_changed event for that posting to jobs.jsonl and leaves preferences.md byte-for-byte unchanged
(c) asks exactly one short question, and asks it because the two readings would keep different postings relevant
(d) states what the wider search costs before it runs or saves anything, then edits search.sources in config.yaml with its comments and shape preserved

evals.scenario: discovery - selected among siblings (search <-> run, search <-> agent)

control.strip: Present the same naive prompt with job-search's trigger description withheld, leaving only the sibling descriptions visible.
control.expectation: With the description present the runner routes the get-started prompt to job-search; the no-guidance control mis-routes to the headless job-search-run or to the operator manual job-search-agent at a measurably higher rate (control_delta > 0).

evals.prompt: A brand-new user with no workspace yet says, naming no skill: 'I'm looking for a new job - can you help me get started?' The sibling skills job-search-run (one headless search pass) and job-search-agent (the operator manual for configuring and troubleshooting the agent) are installed alongside job-search.
expectations: job-search is SELECTED: the front door takes a first-run user from nothing to judged matches
job-search-run is NOT invoked: there is no workspace and no saved query for a headless pass to read
job-search-agent is NOT invoked: the user wants to start, rather than to read how the agent works
The first user-visible message says what is being set up in words a non-expert reads, and carries no numeric score and no credit figures
